title: AgentReady Lab remediation text v0
description: Independently written remediation, keyed by finding code (ADR-0007 section 2). A finding code is a spec-mode assertion id or a compat-mode assertion id, so an entry here joins to exactly one assertion of specs/ruleset.standard.v0.yaml. It is a separate file from the ruleset because the two have different authors, review requirements, licensing exposure, and change cadences, and because specs/checks.v0.yaml is frozen and additionalProperties:false throughout. Only `class` and `summary` reach a report; `detail` is surfaced by the human reporter and by `rules explain`.

remediation_version.description: ADR-0007 section 2's fifth version axis. Moves whenever remediation text changes, independently of the ruleset, the ledger, and the snapshot. A source's pinned version changing in a way that invalidates existing text moves this and the affected rule_version.

ruleset_id.description: The ruleset whose assertion ids these finding codes are. It must equal specs/ruleset.standard.v0.yaml's, for the reason the ruleset's own source_ledger_version must equal the ledger's: a version recorded in one file and never compared with the other is decoration.

ruleset_version.description: The ruleset_version this text was written against, and which the validator holds it equal to.

todo.description: Values an accepted decision requires but does not supply. Never a placeholder for a value that was simply not looked up.

entry.description: One finding code's remediation. Unique on `finding_code` across the file.

finding_code.description: ADR-0002 section 9 makes this identical to a spec.requirements id for a spec-mode finding and to the rule's own versioned compatibility assertion id for a compat-mode finding, so both id shapes are accepted here.

rule_id.description: The rule that declares the assertion. Carried so a reader of this file alone can tell which rule a finding code belongs to; the validator holds it equal to the ruleset's.

class.description: FR-6's three kinds. Fixed by the assertion's strength rather than chosen: a normative assertion derives `fail` and its remediation is a required correction, a recommended or advisory assertion derives `warning` and its remediation is hardening, and only a compatibility assertion, which is a claim about a dated external tool and never about conformance, carries a compatibility workaround.

summary.description: The one line that enters the report, bounded at 240 characters by ADR-0007 section 2. It states the change, not the defect: a summary that restates the assertion tells a reader nothing the message did not.

detail.description: Unbounded prose, surfaced by the human reporter and by `agentready-lab rules explain <rule-id>`, never embedded per finding. Where the pinned source prescribes no fix, this says so; inventing prescriptive advice the source does not support is the failure mode it exists to prevent.

source_refs.description: Ledger identifiers, in the string form specs/checks.v0.yaml uses rather than the ruleset's {source, section} objects. A section pointer belongs to the assertion, which this entry names, and a second copy here would be two pointers that can disagree. ADR-0007 section 4 requires these to resolve against the same registry as the finding's sourceRefs, so the validator additionally holds them to a subset of what the assertion cites: remediation may not rest on a source the requirement it explains does not rest on.

authored_at.description: The date a human wrote or last revised this text. ADR-0007 section 4 forbids generating it at scan time or at any other time without a human author and a review, and this date is where that claim is recorded. Checked for shape only: this file declares no clock of its own, exactly as snapshot.captured_at is bounded by nothing.
